bioAdditions: In the 1790 census Jean appears as 'John Lomereaux' at New Cornwall, Orange Co. (S1). His household held four men aged 16 or over, three women or girls and three enslaved people, so this branch of the family were slaveholders. Two lines above him is Peter Lomereaux, presumably his brother Pierre, who the Davenport genealogy says lived in Cornwall. Further down the same page are Oliver Davenport, his wife Charity's brother, and a David Prindle. FamilySearch's tree of James and Anar Prindle of Newtown includes a son David, born 1757, so the Prindle family may have reached Orange County a generation before Samuel Pringle married into the Lamoreaux family (S1, S2). The Davenport genealogy gives his birth as 31 Dec 1723 in New York City and says he lived in 'Cheesecocks (Monroe)' and died there in 1809 (S3). The site's death date of 28 Nov 1809 may belong to his brother: the same book gives exactly 28 Nov 1809 as the death date at Yorktown, Westchester Co., of his brother Andre (b. 1722). FamilySearch has 24 Jul 1809 instead, without a visible source (S2). FamilySearch also places his burial at Seneca Union Cemetery, Valois, Schuyler Co., NY, which is unlikely for a man who died at Monroe and is unsourced.

conflicts.assessment: The Davenport genealogy gives 28 Nov 1809 for brother Andre at Yorktown and only '1809' for Jean, so the site date may have been borrowed from Andre. Neither date is proven; the will or probate would settle it.

confidenceRecommendation.justification: 1790 census places him beside his Davenport in-laws; the link to Thomas still rests on secondary works and DAR/SAR lineages.
